newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Judicial Commission has sacked Criminal Court Deputy Chief Justice Somchai Udomwong for granting bail to a drug suspect wanted in connection with a record heroin haul in the United States. The decision clears the way for further possible criminal charges against the senior judge as well as disciplinary investigations into other high-ranking court officials implicated in the bail arrangement. (THE NATION)

- Police have arrested the son of a high-ranking military officer after he fired gunshots and took two police officers hostage at a police station. Thanachart Wiwatthanachart opened fire at police station with an M-16 assault rifle, and took two policemen hostage. (BANGKOK POST)

- In an apparent attempt to make the news, first-time Democrat MP Ong-art Klampaiboon demonstrated how to smoke amphetamines in front of TV cameras and an army of reporters. The government has threatened to press criminal charges against him for possession and use of an illegal drug. Even his own party has reprimanded him. (THE NATION)

- The six-member merger group led by Nava Finance and Securities that is seeking a banking licence, have submitted its merger plan to the Bank of Thailand. Under the current merger plan Nava is the sole leader of the group since CMIC Finance and Securities, the co-leader, figured in the Bank of Thailand's list of 16 cash-strapped finance and finance and securities firms. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai commercial banks have provided a state-run finance company with 40 billion baht to safeguard customers of 16 ailing finance houses. The move by 14 members of the Thai Bankers Association came as the government stressed that no more finance companies would be temporarily suspended, as the 75 remaining in operation are financially sound. (BANGKOK POST)
